subject: Maths
subtopic: Dividing quantities in a given ratio
title: Dividing quantities in a given ratio
subtitle: Ratio and Proportion · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can divide a quantity into two or more parts using a given ratio.

key_vocab.definition: Dividing in a ratio means splitting a total into parts whose sizes follow the given ratio.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can divide a quantity into two or more parts using a given ratio.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Dividing in a ratio -- Dividing in a ratio means splitting a total into parts whose sizes follow the given ratio.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Total shares = sum of ratio parts. Value of one share = quantity divided by total shares.
one share = quantity ÷ (a + b)
Then multiply: a shares and b shares

Key examples:
  ✓ £50 in ratio 2 : 3 = £20 and £30  (5 parts, £10 each)
  ✓ 120 in ratio 1 : 2 : 3 = 20, 40, 60  (6 parts, 20 each)
  ✓ Check: shares must add to original total  (20 + 30 = 50 ✓)
  ✗ £50 in ratio 2 : 3 = £25 and £25  (that is halving, not using the ratio)
  ✗ £50 in ratio 2 : 3 = £2 and £3  (must multiply by value of one share)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – two-part ratio
  Divide £80 in the ratio 3 : 5
  Total parts = 3 + 5 = 8
  One part = £80 ÷ 8 = £10
  3 parts = £30, 5 parts = £50
  £30 and £50
  (Check: £30 + £50 = £80.)

Example 2 – three-part ratio
  Divide 180 cm in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4
  Total parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9
  One part = 180 ÷ 9 = 20 cm
  Shares: 40 cm, 60 cm, 80 cm
  40 cm, 60 cm, 80 cm
  (Check: 40 + 60 + 80 = 180.)

sections.title: Two-part ratios
sections.content:
Divide each quantity in the given ratio.

(a) £40 in ratio 1 : 3
(b) 72 in ratio 5 : 4
(c) £120 in ratio 7 : 5
(d) 200 g in ratio 3 : 2

sections.title: Three-part ratios
sections.content:
Divide in the ratio given.

(a) 90 in ratio 1 : 2 : 3
(b) £200 in ratio 2 : 3 : 5
(c) 360 in ratio 4 : 5 : 3
(d) £480 in ratio 1 : 3 : 4

sections.title: Using the difference
sections.content:
Use the difference between shares to solve.

(a) Ratio 2 : 5. Difference is 21. Find each part.
(b) Ratio 3 : 8. Difference is 30. Find each part.
(c) Ratio 1 : 4. Larger part is 60 more. Find each.
(d) Ratio 5 : 9. Difference is 28. Find the total.

sections.title: In context
sections.content:
Solve each word problem.

(a) Cordial : water = 1 : 4. Make 2 litres of drink. How much cordial?
(b) Boys : girls = 3 : 5. There are 32 students. How many boys?
(c) Cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 2 : 4. Need 35 kg total. Find each.
(d) Savings : spending = 2 : 7. Earn £270 per week. How much saved?

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Solve each ratio problem.

(a) £450 in ratio 4 : 5
(b) Ratio 3 : 7. Larger part is £84. Find the smaller.
(c) 720 ml in ratio 1 : 2 : 5
(d) Two numbers in ratio 5 : 8. Sum is 78. Find both.
(e) £600 split in ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Largest share?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To divide £60 in ratio 1 : 2, find total parts (3), then one part (£20)
✗ Dividing £60 in ratio 1 : 2 gives £30 and £30
✓ The shares must always add up to the original quantity
✗ Ratio 3 : 5 means the first share is always £3
✓ If ratio is 2 : 3 and difference is 10, one part = 10
